sentence: A 25-year-old patient who, during admission to the Internal Medicine service due to evening fever of 3 days' duration, was incidentally discovered by ultrasound study to have a tumor in the right testicle.
As a personal history, she reports not having any drug allergies.
Bilateral inguinal herniorrhaphy.
She reports a painless tumor that has been going on for a year and has been progressively increasing.
On physical examination, an enlargement of the right testicle with a painless tumor in the upper pole was palpable.
If a testicular tumor is suspected, different complementary tests are performed.
In the testicular ultrasound, a heterogeneous, solid tumor was seen in the right testicle measuring 78 mm x 57 mm x 61 mm, compatible with a primary testicular tumor.
Normal left testis.
Computerized axial tomography (CT): right testicular tumor with retrocaval and para-aortic lymphadenopathy > 2 and <5 cm.
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH): 1890 IU/I; alpha-fetoprotein (AFP): 51 ng/ml; beta-chorionic gonadotropin (Beta-HCG): 23 mIU/ml.
He underwent a right inguinal orchiectomy with a Pathological Anatomy report of a 7 cm Embryonal Carcinoma that replaced the parenchyma and epididymis with cord implants and reached the albuginea.

Diagnosed with embryonal carcinoma of the right testicle T3N2M0, stage II with intermediate risk due to elevated LDH, he completed treatment with chemotherapy according to the BEP (bleom<icin, etoposide and cisplatin) scheme for 4 cycles.
At 4 years old, and being free of disease in the follow-up check-ups, she went to the emergency room due to a painful tumor in the left testicle.
Physical examination revealed a left monorchium and an indurated tumor at the lower pole of the left epididymis.
Among the complementary examinations, the following stand out: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH): 347 IU/I; alpha-fetoprotein (AFP): 2.4 ng/ml; beta-chorionic gonadotropin (Beta-HCG): 0.1 mIU/ml.
Chest x-ray: No pathological findings.
Testicular ultrasound: Testicular tumor measuring 51x19x22 mm in size, with heterogeneous echostructure and color Doppler flow, which also affects the body and tail of the epididymis.
Calcification in the anteroinferior aspect of the testicle.
Thoraco-abdomino-pelvic Axial Computerized Tomography: Normal liver, spleen and pancreas.
Kidneys of normal morphology and density.
No lymphadenopathy or lymph node chains.

Under the suspicion of a second germ cell tumor, a left radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed, the Pathological Anatomy resulting in a classic Seminoma of 3.2 cm in diameter that infiltrated the testicular parenchyma, extending to the epididymis and spermatic cord.
The postoperative period was uneventful.
He was referred to the Oncology Service for evaluation of adjuvant treatment and control.
Given that the maximum diameter of the tumor is 3.2 cm and does not affect the rete testis, conservative control treatment is chosen.

Three months later, in a control Axial Computed Tomography, an enlarged left retroperitoneal adenopathy (3.5 cm) was detected, with a poor separation plane with the psoas that traps the middle third of the ureter causing grade I hydronephrosis.

In the blood tests control: blood count, biochemistry and hemostasis within normal parameters except for Creatinine of 1.2 mg/dl; lactate dehydrogenase=552 IU/I, alpha-fetoprotein and beta-chorionic gonadotropin within normal limits.
He was diagnosed with retroperitoneal recurrence and underwent treatment with chemotherapy (etoposide and cisplatin for 4 cycles).
Currently, the patient has been disease-free for 3 years in the periodic check-ups carried out in the Urology and Oncology services.
